review_status: draft v1 - giant oceanic pelagic profile

profile.behavior: Massive pelagic migrator that travels along deep oceanic fronts and Gulf Stream boundaries.

factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, cool oceanic water favored by bluefin tuna.
factors.value_notes: Archival-tag data report Atlantic bluefin tuna occupying 10–23 °C for most of the record, with peak occupancy around 13–20 °C; ICCAT analyses report broad adult and juvenile temperature ranges. This supports the configured 12–24 °C range and 16–22 °C ideal as broad species-level conditions, but temperature use varies by stock, life stage, season, and dive depth; it is not a single South Florida SST optimum.

factors.reason_template: Thermal break strength is {per10km} C per 10 km, marking oceanic fronts.
factors.value_notes: NOAA's habitat guidance describes bluefin feeding along productive frontal features, including chlorophyll-a fronts, and tracking changing water temperature and currents. This supports frontal habitat association, but a chlorophyll front is not identical to the runtime SST-gradient magnitude and does not calibrate a higher-is-better score.

factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, in open ocean pelagic waters.
factors.value_notes: NOAA reports bluefin tuna frequently diving to 500–1,000 m; archival tags document broad vertical use. These are fish dive depths, not seafloor bathymetry. Bluefin are highly migratory and occupy both shelf and open-ocean habitats, so these sources do not validate the configured 100–3,000 m bathymetric band or 200–1,500 m ideal. Depth remains an active gate.

value_text.peak: It is peak bluefin tuna winter/spring migration season.

factors.value_notes: NOAA reports western Atlantic bluefin spawning from mid-April through June, mainly in the Gulf of Mexico, while NOAA EFH tagging summaries describe seasonal movements and shifting depth/temperature use. The configured January–May window may represent winter-to-spring migration/availability, but it does not match the full Gulf spawning period and needs local catch/telemetry calibration.

text.day: It is full daylight, when fish feed actively.
text.dawn: It is dawn, a low-light time when fish feed actively.
text.dusk: It is dusk, a low-light time when fish feed actively.

timing.note: Patterns reported by local captains and fishing writers, not tested by studies.
